prompt.context: Lion King Bank is a consumer bank in South Africa providing checking, savings, credit cards, loans, etc. They have branches in all 9 South African provinces. They have completed an aggressive cost-cutting program, but revenues are still low and profitability is also low. They are looking to fix this and improve profitability quickly, and they have come to us to help them find a solution.
prompt.question: How does the client improve profitability quickly?

clarifying_info.q: Has the competitive landscape changed recently?
clarifying_info.a: Nothing has changed about the competitive landscape recently.

clarifying_info.q: What is the primary lever available given costs are already cut?
clarifying_info.a: The focus should be on revenue improvement.

exhibits.title: Student Banking Market Sizing
exhibits.shows: A table with rows for Youth population, % students, % using banking, LKB share, and Number of accounts. The Current Year 1 column has some values filled in. The Year 3 projected column and CAGR column have some fields blank for the candidate to calculate.

framework: Product Mix: assess existing product mix and expansion opportunities
Customers: analyze segments (students vs. affluent mid-income), demographics, growth opportunities, revenue potential, acquisition and retention
Revenues: focus on two levers — number of accounts and money earned per account
Competition: benchmark fees and product offerings against competitors

questions.prompt: What are the main strategies to dramatically increase revenues within 2 years?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify two primary levers: (1) increase number of customer accounts, and (2) increase money made from existing customers. Strong answers also mention expanding into alternative markets. Key insight: since costs are already cut, revenue is the only path to profitability improvement.

questions.prompt: There are two customer segments under evaluation: students and affluent mid-income customers. They already have many mid-income customers and are looking at expanding student customers. How would you evaluate the student market and how might you target students? (Use Exhibit 1)
questions.guidance: Candidate should size the student market using Exhibit 1, showing year-3 account projections. Should also propose ways to reach the student population such as campus branding, student-friendly products, and targeting parents with existing accounts.

math.setup: Use the table to calculate Year 3 student accounts at LKB. Youth population grows at 10% CAGR for 2 years, then apply % students (doubling from 10% to 20%), % using banking (50% to 75%), and LKB share (10% to 20%).
math.answer: From 25,000 accounts today to ~181,500 accounts in Year 3 — a ~7x increase in student accounts.

questions.prompt: Research shows students can only be acquired through heavy price discounts. Should the company focus on student accounts or affluent mid-income accounts?
questions.guidance: Key insight: despite high growth in account numbers, student accounts will NOT translate into immediate revenue growth because LKB cannot earn significant fees from heavily discounted student accounts. Since the goal is to improve revenues QUICKLY, student accounts are not viable in the short term. Candidate should recommend focusing on affluent mid-income customers now, while acknowledging the long-term value of students (high lifetime value, high switching costs later).

brainstorming.prompt: How should Lion King Bank target and acquire affluent mid-income customers?

categories.name: Product improvements
ideas: Add mutual fund and fixed-income account products
Improve product attractiveness through lower fees

categories.name: Customer acquisition from competition
ideas: Evaluate product mix against competitors and improve offerings
Lower fees or interest rates to attract competitor customers

categories.name: Existing customer monetization
ideas: Cross-sell more products to existing customer base

categories.name: Student long-term strategy
ideas: Campus branding and tie-ups, locate branches near campuses
Offer student loans and low/no-fee accounts with low balance requirements
Target parents with existing accounts to acquire student children

recommendation: Lion King Bank should focus on the affluent mid-income segment to aggressively increase revenue in the short term
Target these customers by improving product range (e.g., mutual funds, fixed income) and product attractiveness, combined with aggressive sales and direct marketing
risks: Aggressively acquiring mid-income customers from competitors may trigger price wars on fees and interest rates
Cannot afford to ignore the student segment entirely — students have high lifetime value and bank-switching costs are high later in life, so ignoring them now risks losing a large future cohort
next_steps: In-depth analysis of product mix to identify optimization opportunities
Evaluate how to convert student customers into profitable customers over time
Identify new sources of revenue including geographic expansion
